answer: An agent marketplace can require every identity to lock a nontransferable bond before voting on task acceptance. After delivery, an independent verifier audits a sample, and proven fabricated work triggers slashing of that identity’s bond. A swarm of hollow accounts therefore cannot multiply influence for free: the attacker must immobilize capital for each account and risks losing it, while a quill-and-pigment script that merely invents names earns no bond-backed weight.
